quests.title: Missile Materials
desc: So you want to throw a bomb at something a thousand blocks away. Welcome to the ICBM program. A GregGuns missile is not one crafting recipe: it's a §lMissile Body§r and a §lWarhead§r, built separately from GregTech parts and Galacticraft rocket hardware, then stacked on a launch pad and fired from a Launch Control.

This chapter walks the Tier 1 build part by part, the way the [quest]Space Race[/quest] tab walks the Tier 1 rocket. Start by stocking the materials almost every part shares. Advanced circuits go into the Missile Chip (2), the Guidance Computer (1), the Fuze Assembly (1) and the Launch Control (2). Stainless steel plates are the warhead casing, and steel plates go into the computer and the fuze. Nothing in the ICBM program runs below HV, so your HV Assembler and Circuit Assembler will be busy.
Then work through the part quests below: chip and schematic, compressed plates, fins, engine and guidance for the body, a fuze for the warhead. Check NEI on every part.
[note]The ICBM chapter needs Galacticraft and the ICBM module (config modules.icbm). If you already hold a finished Missile Body T1, the body's part quests complete themselves.[/note]

quests.title: Missile Chip
desc: Every missile starts as a chip. The Missile Chip T1 holds the flight program, and it's the first thing the NASA Workbench will ask about.

Make it in the GregTech Circuit Assembler at HV (20 seconds) from a Plastic Circuit Board, 2 Advanced circuits and 4 fine gold wires. Check NEI for the exact recipe. The chip is only half the job: the next quest engraves it into a schematic.

quests.title: Engrave the Schematic
desc: A Galacticraft NASA Workbench builds whatever its schematic tells it to. The Missile Schematic T1 opens the missile's own page, with slots in the shape of the missile.

Put the chip and a red lens in the Laser Engraver at HV (30 seconds); the lens is not used up. Slot the finished schematic into the NASA Workbench and use the Next button to find the missile page. Check NEI for the lens.
[note]Each missile tier has its own chip and schematic. A Tier 2 schematic never opens the Tier 1 page.[/note]

quests.title: Compressed Steel Airframe
desc: The missile's airframe is a column of three compressed steel plates, the same Galacticraft plates the rocket program uses.

Compressed plates come from the Implosion Compressor: a steel plate plus an explosive charge. Check NEI for the charge it takes. Make three; the body page has exactly three plate slots in one vertical column.

quests.title: Rocket Fins
desc: A missile is a rocket that doesn't come back, so it flies on rocket fins. The body takes four Galacticraft Tier 1 Rocket Fins, one in each fin slot, the same fins the Tier 1 rocket uses.
In this pack the fins are made from compressed steel and heavy-duty plates. Check NEI, or the [quest]Space Race[/quest] tab, which walks the rocket parts too.

quests.title: Rocket Engine
desc: The Tier 1 missile burns the same engine as the Galacticraft Tier 1 rocket. It's the priciest single part of the body, so take your time with it.
The pack's engine recipe uses SDHD120 and heavy-duty plates, a fuel canister, a firebox casing and a detector. Check NEI for the current recipe. One engine per body.

quests.title: Guidance Computer
desc: The Guidance Computer tells the missile where to come down. The Mk I is the base computer for a Tier 1 body; better computers land closer.

Make the Mk I in the Assembler at HV from an Advanced circuit, a steel plate and 4 fine copper wires. A Mk II (EV) gives a Tier 1 body one step of guidance and a Mk III (IV) two, so the missile scatters less. You can fit a better computer into a finished body later in the Assembler. Check NEI.

quests.title: Fuze Assembly
desc: Every Tier 1 warhead starts as an inert casing, and a Fuze Assembly Mk I is built into it: the timer and trigger that make the charges go off when and where you want, and nothing before that.

It's an Assembler recipe at HV from an Advanced circuit, a steel plate and 4 fine copper wires, the same shopping list as the Guidance Computer. Check NEI. Make a few: every Inert T1 Warhead takes one, and so do the HV launcher warheads.

quests.title: Plastic Explosive
desc: Every warhead's explosive is Plastic Explosive: one piece is one charge. More charges make a wider, harder blast, though each extra charge adds a little less than the one before.
The Assembler makes 4 at HV from 2 PTFE plates and 2 Industrial TNT. Check NEI. That's the only place Industrial TNT goes; a warhead takes the charges and nothing else explosive.
Make five, enough to fill a Tier 1 casing. Heavier casings hold 20, 64 and finally 128, so it's worth automating early.
[warn]Plastic Explosive is safe in a chest. Once it's loaded into a warhead it isn't.[/warn]

quests.title: Inert Warhead
desc: A warhead is built in steps, and the first is an empty one. The Inert T1 Warhead is a stainless steel casing with a Fuze Assembly Mk I wired into it. There is no explosive inside yet, so it is perfectly safe: it can't be placed, launched or set off, and a silo won't take it.

The Assembler makes it at HV from 4 stainless steel plates and a Fuze Assembly Mk I, on programmed circuit 2. Check NEI. Every heavier casing follows the same pattern at its own tier: titanium and a Mk II fuze at EV, then tungstensteel, naquadria and neutronium with a Mk III.
From here you customize it. Fit a payload in the Assembler if you want a special blast, then load Plastic Explosive charges to make it live. A Tier 1 casing takes up to 5 charges.
[note]An inert warhead looks like the real thing, only darker. Read the tooltip: it shows the payload and Charges: 0.[/note]

quests.title: Choose a Payload
desc: A plain warhead just goes bang. A payload changes what the bang does: steel fragments, a lead mass, napalm, a dizzying or choking gas, smoke, or a field generator that pushes everything away or pulls it in.

The Assembler fits a payload at HV: put one bare Inert T1 Warhead in with the payload's parts and the right programmed circuit, and you get the same inert warhead with that payload, ready for charges. The Shrapnel payload, for example, is one Steel Fragmentation Sleeve. Check NEI for every payload and its circuit.
[note]A payload holds no explosive. You still load Plastic Explosive afterwards. Fitting a new payload to a casing that already has one replaces the old payload.[/note]

quests.title: Missile Body
desc: Time to put the airframe together. With the Missile Schematic T1 slotted, the NASA Workbench's missile page shows the slots on a rocket outline: three compressed steel plates down the middle, four fins at the bottom, the engine at the base and the guidance computer beside the nose.

Fill every slot and take the Missile Body T1 from the result slot. It uses one item from each slot. There is no warhead slot: the warhead goes on the body later, on the launch pad. A Tier 1 body flies 20 to 1,000 blocks and needs 2,000 mB of fuel.
Hand-building comes first, and it never stops working. Once the parts flow, your HV Assembler builds the same body without the workbench: see [quest]Automate the Body[/quest].

quests.title: Your First Warhead
desc: Now make it live. Put an Inert T1 Warhead and 1 to 8 Plastic Explosive in a crafting grid and you get a live T1 warhead with that many charges, up to its cap of 5. A bare casing with charges alone is a Condensed warhead, plain high explosive. A casing with a payload becomes that blast type.

Put the warhead back in the grid with more Plastic Explosive to top it up; a load that would pass the cap simply doesn't craft, so nothing is wasted. For automation, the Assembler fills a whole casing at once: an inert warhead and 5 Plastic Explosive on the blast's circuit. Check NEI.
The tooltip shows the charges, the blast radius and the center damage. Make one warhead, any type, any fill.
[warn]A warhead is a live explosive block. Fire, redstone and nearby explosions all set it off.[/warn]

quests.title: Launch Pad
desc: A missile launches from a Galacticraft launch pad: nine pad blocks in a 3 by 3 square. You may already have one from the rocket program.

Right-click the pad with the body; whichever pad block you click, it stands in the middle. Then place the warhead on its nose, where it seats flush. Sneak and right-click the body with an empty hand to arm it, which turns the stack into one missile. A warhead heavier than the body's tier is refused at arming.
[note]Changed your mind? Sneak and right-click the armed missile with an empty hand: it drops the body and the warhead, and the fuel is lost.[/note]

quests.title: Fuel the Missile
desc: The missile's tank starts empty and only fills while it stands on the pad. Attach a Galacticraft Fuel Loader to the pad and feed it rocket fuel.

A Tier 1 missile takes 2,000 mB of Cetane-Boosted Diesel or RP-1, or a better rocket fuel; plain Galacticraft fuel is refused. It won't launch until the tank is full. Fuel left unburned at impact makes the blast up to 25 percent wider, so a close target hits harder than a far one.

quests.title: Launch Control
desc: The Launch Control is the button. It's a GregTech single block at HV, made in the Assembler from an HV machine hull, an HV sensor, an HV emitter, an empty data stick and 2 Advanced circuits. Check NEI.

Set it against one edge of the pad, level with it (corners don't count, the way Galacticraft's own launch controller attaches), and power it at HV. Type the target X and Z, press Use My Position, or load a target from a data stick (Save and Load target buttons). The screen shows the range (at least 20 blocks, at most 1,000 for Tier 1) and the blast radius to expect.

quests.title: First Launch
desc: Everything comes together here: a Missile Body, a warhead and a Launch Control, with the pad and the fuel loader you already built. Hold all three to finish the quest, then go and fire it.

Stack the missile on the pad, arm it, fill the tank and set a target. Press Launch, or give the Launch Control a redstone pulse. A 10-second countdown starts, and Abort still stands the missile down, armed and fueled. After ignition there's no turning back: the missile climbs, flies its arc and detonates on impact. A Tier 1 flight at full range takes about a minute. The pad, the fuel loader and the Launch Control come through unharmed.
Next: a Tier 2 missile, radar and air defense, and the Missile Silo.
[warn]Make sure nobody stands at the target, you included. A missile that is shot down still goes off where it is hit.[/warn]

quests.title: Automate the Body
desc: One missile is a demonstration. Twenty is a policy. The NASA Workbench is fine for your first body, but filling slots by hand gets old fast, so let a GregTech machine do it: your plain §lHV Assembler§r builds Missile Bodies with no research and no data stick.

The Assembler takes the same parts as the workbench page: three compressed steel plates, four Tier 1 rocket fins and a Tier 1 rocket engine. In place of the guidance computer it wires in 2 Advanced circuits, and it wants 250 L of lubricant in its fluid slot. A Tier 1 body takes 30 seconds at HV. The Tier 2 body works the same way in an EV Assembler: four compressed titanium plates, Tier 2 fins and engine, 2 Data circuits, the same lubricant, 45 seconds. Check NEI.

A machine-built body has no guidance steps. To make it land closer, put the body and a better Guidance Computer back in the Assembler: 15 seconds at the body's voltage, and the same body comes out guided. Build four Tier 1 bodies.
[note]The Tier 1 body needs HV power, so an LV or MV Assembler won't run it, and a Tier 2 body needs an EV one.[/note]

quests.title: Tier 3 on the Assembly Line
desc: The Tier 3 missile is the big one: six blocks tall, 8,000 mB of rocket fuel, 20 to 8,000 blocks of range (10,000 from a silo), and the only body that carries the heaviest casings, antimatter and red matter included. It launches only from a Missile Silo with a LuV Energy Hatch.

Build the first one by hand. The Tier 3 chip comes from the Circuit Assembler at LuV (a Multifiberglass board, 2 Master circuits and 8 fine platinum wires) and is engraved with a yellow lens. The NASA Workbench page takes four compressed titanium plates, four Heavy Duty Rocket Fins Tier 3, a Heavy Duty Rocket Engine Tier 3 and a Guidance Computer Mk III, which fits but gives no guidance steps on a body this heavy.

This is the one missile body built on GregTech's §lAssembly Line§r. Scan a hand-built Missile Body T3 onto a data stick in the Scanner (180 seconds at LuV) to unlock the recipe. The line then builds it from the same plates, fins and engine, 2 Master circuits and 250 L of lubricant in 60 seconds at LuV. Check NEI. Build two Tier 3 bodies.
[note]Keep one hand-built body aside for the scan. The Tier 1 and Tier 2 bodies never need the Assembly Line: the Assembler builds those.[/note]

quests.title: Demolition Charge
desc: A warhead doesn't need a missile. Place it where you want the hole and light it with Flint and Steel, a Fire Charge or a redstone pulse. The fuse is 3 seconds plus 1 second per 3 blocks of blast radius, so a full Condensed warhead gives you 6 seconds to leave.

Fill a Condensed warhead to its cap of 5 charges for the biggest hole a Tier 1 casing makes: in a crafting grid, or all at once in the Assembler from a bare Inert T1 Warhead and 5 Plastic Explosive on circuit 1. Keep a lighter with it.
[warn]Get well clear, and keep other charges away: another explosion sets a warhead off in half a second.[/warn]

quests.title: De-arming
desc: Built the wrong warhead, or want the parts back? Every step of the chain runs backwards. Put a live warhead and a Defuse Kit in a crafting grid: each craft takes out up to 8 Plastic Explosive, whole, for one use of the kit. The last charge out leaves the inert warhead with its payload, ready for a different load.
The Cutting Machine does the rest at the warhead's own tier: it empties a full warhead in one go, takes a payload out and cuts a bare casing back into its plates and Fuze Assembly. Check NEI.
Unload a T1 warhead until only the inert casing is left.
[note]A payload's parts come back, but any fluid it held is spent. A Macerator or Arc Furnace only gives back a warhead's metal.[/note]

quests.title: Titanium Casing
desc: The Tier 2 casing is titanium and holds up to 20 charges, four times the Tier 1 casing. The Assembler makes the Inert T2 Warhead at EV from 8 titanium plates and a Fuze Assembly Mk II. The Mk II fuze is itself an EV Assembler recipe from a Data circuit, a titanium plate and 4 fine electrum wires.

A Tier 2 casing needs a payload before it takes charges: Fragmentation (a titanium Fragmentation Sleeve), Thermobaric (canisters of kerosene), Sonic, Breaching or Contagious, each fitted in the Assembler at EV. Then load 20 Plastic Explosive, in the Assembler or a few at a time in a crafting grid. Check NEI. Make a Tier 2 warhead.
[warn]Tier 2 blasts reach much farther than Tier 1. Read the tooltip's radius before you place one.[/warn]

quests.title: Launcher Warhead
desc: Your shoulder launchers can carry a blast type too. A Launcher Warhead is a small charge: High Explosive, Heavy Slug, Incendiary and Phosphorus at HV and Demolition at EV for the Rocket Launcher and Grim Reaper; Grenade HE (HV) and Grenade Cluster (EV) for the Grenade Launcher; EMP (LuV) for the Nuke Launcher.

Craft it with the launcher in the crafting grid for 4 charges, up to 16. Each shot spends one charge and the launcher's own round, and goes off as a small blast; its center damage is capped at 1.25 times the launcher's own. Make a High Explosive one; check NEI for its recipe.
[warn]Keep your distance from the impact point: these rounds hurt you as much as your target.[/warn]

quests.title: Tier 2 Missile
desc: Tier 2 flies up to 3,000 blocks and carries a titanium-cased warhead (or a lighter one). The build follows the Tier 1 path one step up.

The Tier 2 chip is made at EV from an Advanced Circuit Board (the epoxy one), 2 Data circuits and 4 fine electrum wires, and engraved with a blue lens. The body page takes four compressed titanium plates, four Heavy Rocket Fins, a Heavy Rocket Engine and a Guidance Computer Mk II or better. It burns 4,000 mB of Dense Hydrazine or a better rocket fuel. Check NEI. Build a Tier 2 body. After that, your EV Assembler builds more of them from the same plates, fins and engine, 2 Data circuits and 250 L of lubricant.
[note]The Heavy Rocket Fins and Engine are Galacticraft parts built from Tier 3 Heavy Duty Plates. This quest opens once you finish the Space Race quests for both.[/note]

quests.title: Missile Silo
desc: The Missile Silo is a GregTech multiblock that loads, fuels and fires missiles for you. A silo shot flies 25 percent farther and scatters half as much as a pad shot.

Build a 5 by 5 tower around an open 3 by 3 shaft: a Galacticraft launch pad for the shaft floor in a ring of Light or Dark Concrete, three rings of clear glass (Tinkers' Construct or EnderIO), seven rings of concrete (any finish but cobblestone) and a rim of 12 Gantry Beams. The HV controller sits in the middle glass ring. Fit an Input Bus, an Input Hatch for fuel, an Energy Hatch and a Maintenance Hatch in place of wall, glass or floor-ring blocks. Check the controller's hologram.

The Energy Hatch sets what it launches: HV for Tier 1, EV for Tier 2, LuV for Tier 3. Feed the bus a body and a warhead and it stands the missile in the shaft. Build a Launch Control into the silo in place of any wall, glass or floor-ring block, one per silo: it fires that silo and no other, and its screen names the silo.

quests.title: Abandoned Silo Complex
desc: Old missile bases lie buried in the Overworld and on every planet with solid ground. A complex is about 240 by 240 blocks and 24 blocks down: a hub, wide halls, 35 to 40 rooms and a gallery of four to ten real silos. On the surface you see only concrete shafts, sometimes a small radar hut, and an escape-ladder trapdoor.

Nothing in a complex is better than its planet's ceiling: EV in the Overworld and on the Moon, one voltage tier more for each rocket tier above. Bring back proof: a block of Silo Complex Wall, or a damaged missile body from a salvage chest. The damaged body can't be placed or flown, but it recycles for its plates.
[warn]Every complex has guards at its posts: a couple in an abandoned one, many in an operational one. A post you break stays broken.[/warn]

quests.title: Take Over a Silo
desc: Every silo in a complex is a real Missile Silo with its hatches in place, missing exactly one part: a concrete block where the controller goes, or a glass block under it where the Energy Hatch goes.

Look for the part in the Safe, Stockpile, Workshop and Control chests, or craft it. Put it in and the silo forms. A found Energy Hatch is EV, which launches up to Tier 2; swap in a LuV hatch for Tier 3. Power it and fire it from its own Launch Control, in the top row of the silo's window: the complex's silo is yours. Bring back the part you found.
[warn]Clear the guard posts before you start working on the silo.[/warn]

quests.title: Radar Station
desc: The radar huts on a complex's surface hold a small radar with its Energy Hatch left out, so they sit dark.

Mine the Radar Casing under the radar controller, put an HV Energy Hatch in its place and power it. The radar forms and its dish starts to turn. Link it to an air-defense battery with a data stick, as for any radar. Hold the Radar Casing you mined out and an HV Energy Hatch to finish the quest.

quests.title: Nuclear Warhead
desc: The nuclear warhead is a Tier 3 casing, two blocks tall. Start with an Inert T3 Warhead (the Assembler at LuV: 8 tungstensteel plates and a Fuze Assembly Mk III), fit the nuclear payload at ZPM (8 uranium-235 ingots and 4 plutonium ingots), then load 64 Plastic Explosive, its implosion lens. It flies only on a Tier 3 missile, from the silo. Check NEI.
A full warhead blasts 64 blocks, and nothing living inside the inner 60 percent (38 blocks at full fill) survives, bosses included. The top layer of ground is left irradiated for about an hour.
[warn]Cross the blast zone only in full hazmat armor, and stand well back from the launch target. There is no safe distance inside the inner radius.[/warn]

quests.title: Fallout Cleanup
desc: A nuclear blast leaves irradiated earth, hot earth near ground zero, trinitite and a little fallout goo. Mine it out in full hazmat armor.

Trinitite Shards are macerated at HV into Crushed Trinitite, which a Centrifuge at HV turns into dusts. Goo is dissolved in 1,000 L of nitric acid in a Chemical Reactor at LuV, then centrifuged at EV. While goo stands in a chunk its ground never heals, so dig it up. Make Crushed Trinitite.
[warn]Irradiated ground hurts without full hazmat armor.[/warn]

quests.title: Antidote
desc: The Antidote is a syringe for the bad days. The Assembler makes 2 at HV from a rubber plate, a stainless steel plate and 2 charcoal dust. Check NEI.

Hold use for 1.6 seconds and it cures poison, hunger, weakness, slowness, nausea, mining fatigue and radiation at once, then guards you against them for 3 minutes. Armor still has to keep the cause off, and it does nothing against fire or explosions. Make one.

quests.title: Antimatter
desc: Antimatter is the Tier 4 casing: naquadria plates, two blocks tall, up to 128 charges. The Assembler makes the Inert T4 Warhead at UV from 8 naquadria plates and a Fuze Assembly Mk III, fits the antimatter payload at UV (2 UV Field Generators, a Quantum Eye and 4 plutonium-241 ingots), and fills it with 128 Plastic Explosive. Check NEI.

A full warhead blasts 80 blocks, and nothing living in the inner 48 survives, bosses included. It leaves no fallout, and it ends any Red Matter within 200 blocks. The Tier 3 missile carries it from the silo. Make one.
[warn]Bosses are not safe and neither are you. Launch it from far away.[/warn]

quests.title: Red Matter
desc: Red Matter is the Tier 5 casing and the end of the line. The Assembler makes the Inert T5 Warhead at UHV from 8 neutronium plates and a Fuze Assembly Mk III, fits the red matter payload at UHV (2 UHV Field Generators, 2 Quantum Eyes and 2 UHV Emitters), and fills it with 128 Plastic Explosive. Check NEI.

It digs no crater. A black ball grows from a radius of 2 to 32 blocks at a full casing, eating blocks, killing everything inside (bosses too) and pulling in what is near. It idles for 10 seconds once full-grown and lives 60 seconds at most, a server setting. An Antimatter blast ends it at once. Make one.
[warn]Nothing inside the ball survives. Keep an Antimatter warhead ready if you ever need to stop one.[/warn]

quests.title: Ender Warhead
desc: The Ender warhead is a Tier 3 casing. Fit the ender payload to an Inert T3 Warhead in the Assembler at LuV (a LuV Emitter and 16 Eyes of Ender), then load up to 64 Plastic Explosive charges. Check NEI.

It digs no crater. For 8 seconds it pulls every living thing within 24 blocks toward the center, and anything that reaches the middle (within 4 blocks) is sent to one landing spot 40 to 128 blocks away, up to 64 per blast. Bosses are pulled but never sent. It flies only from the silo. Make one.
[warn]The landing spot is random. Don't stand in the pull unless you want to go too.[/warn]

quests.title: Anti-Gravitational Warhead
desc: The other exotic Tier 3 warhead takes the anti-gravitational payload, fitted to an Inert T3 Warhead in the Assembler at LuV (2 LuV Field Generators and 4 Nether Stars), then up to 64 Plastic Explosive charges. Check NEI.

For 30 seconds it lifts up to 512 plain blocks within 20 blocks off the ground, top layer first, and floats the living things there. Machines and chests stay put, and every lifted block lands again or drops as an item. Make one.
[warn]What goes up comes down. Anything floating when the effect ends falls.[/warn]

quests.title: Radar
desc: Other people have missiles too. A radar watches every missile in flight and flags the ones that will land inside its protected radius, which you set on its screen (64 blocks to begin with).

The radar is a small 3 by 3 build of Radar Casing, two high, with one casing on top for the dish. The Assembler makes the casing four at a time at HV from 6 stainless steel plates. The HV controller sees 128 blocks and the EV controller 256, at any height; put an Energy Hatch of its tier and a Maintenance Hatch in the base. Its redstone output on every side is the number of incoming missiles, up to 15. Right-click the controller with a data stick to save its link for a battery. Build a radar.

quests.title: Radar Tower
desc: When 256 blocks isn't enough warning, build the Radar Tower: a 3 by 3 tower of Radar Casing, 7 blocks tall, with a Gantry Beam mast up the middle and a dish turning on top.

Its range comes from its weakest Energy Hatch: 512 blocks at IV, 768 at LuV, 1,024 at ZPM, 1,280 at UV and 1,536 at UHV. Put an Energy Hatch and a Maintenance Hatch in the bottom ring, and set the protected radius from the R button on the controller screen. Build the controller; check NEI.

quests.title: Air-Defense Battery
desc: A radar tells you a missile is coming; the Air-Defense Battery does something about it. It holds 4 stacks of 16 SAMs and a data stick.

Put a stick that carries a radar's link in its slot and it fires by itself at the nearest threat that radar reports within 256 blocks: one SAM a second at most, 400 EU each. A SAM does 40 damage, so Tier 1 and Tier 2 missiles fall to one and a Tier 3 missile takes two. Check NEI for both recipes. Make a battery and a SAM.
[warn]The warhead goes off where the missile is hit, so shoot early, well away from your base.[/warn]

quests.title: EMP Tower
desc: The EMP Tower sends one pulse when you press Fire, on a redstone rising edge or from a computer. You pick the radius, 4 to 100 blocks, and the pulse costs 25 EU per square block of radius: 90,000 EU at 60. It's an EV Assembler recipe; check NEI.

The pulse drains the 64 nearest machines, batteries and Battery Buffers to zero and gives each multiblock one maintenance issue. A missile in range is destroyed 50 percent of the time, has its guidance fried 40 percent of the time and has its warhead set off 1 percent of the time.
[warn]The pulse doesn't care whose machines it drains. Keep the tower away from your own base.[/warn]

quests.title: Handheld Tools
desc: Three tools for the field. The Radar Gun aims 200 blocks and stores that spot as a target; right-click a Launch Control to copy it in. The Remote Detonator links to a placed warhead when you sneak-click it, and a right-click lights its fuse from 128 blocks (HV), 256 (EV) or 512 (IV).

The Defuse Kit puts a lit fuse out (right-click), or takes apart a missile standing on a pad or in a silo (left-click) before its countdown starts; it lasts 32 uses. Check NEI for the recipes. Make all three.
[warn]A lit fuse doesn't wait for you. Defuse fast or run.[/warn]

quests.title: Golden Dome
desc: Prefer a computer at the controls? The Golden Dome is a yellow OpenComputers floppy with ready-made programs, made in the Assembler at HV from a blank floppy and a Good circuit. Check NEI.

Put it in a computer's disk drive and link your machines through an OpenComputers Adapter. The launch program fires a missile (it always asks first), radarwatch lists radar contacts with an alarm, autodefense fires your batteries at incoming missiles, and emp runs the EMP tower. Build an Adapter to wire it up.
